Complications include hypoxia leading to pertussis encephalopathy and severe pneumonia; critical cases can be fatal and survivors may have lasting sequelae. articleHeadline: Rat hepatitis E virus may be a hidden cause of hepatitis in humans
articleSummary: Rat hepatitis E virus (ratHEV, Rocahepevirus ratti) is increasingly recognized as a zoonotic cause of hepatitis in humans. Genotypes C1–C5 exist; C1 carries zoonotic potential, while C2–C5 appear to have limited zoonosis. Domestic pigs can transiently harbor ratHEV; serology shows exposure in Asia and Europe. Diagnosis relies on viral RNA by qPCR; antibody assays show cross-reactivity and limited utility. Clinically, ratHEV can range from subclinical hepatitis to fulminant liver failure, with chronic hepatitis in immunocompromised individuals; encephalitis reported. Limited assays imply an underestimated global burden.

articleSummary: Ophiocordyceps unilateralis, the zombie fungus, is a relentless parasite in tropical forests, hijacking carpenter ants (Camponotus) to reproduce. A spore infects a forager, penetrates the exoskeleton, and multiplies in the hemolymph as yeast-like cells. Rather than the brain, the fungus infiltrates muscles, creating a chemical-driven network that overrides the host’s behavior. Under this control, the ant leaves the colony and climbs vegetation to about 25 cm above the ground, where humidity and temperature favor fungal growth, then bites a leaf vein in a fatal death grip. Weeks later, a fruiting stalk (stroma) emerges from the ant’s head, laden with spore bulbs that rain onto the forest floor. Mortality after infection is 100%, with host specificity to Camponotus ants, and alkaloids/enterotoxins modulating peripheral nerves. The fungus poses no risk to humans; higher mammalian body temperatures prevent infection, though related species inspire immunosuppressive and antitumor compounds.

articleSummary: Ehrlichiosis in dogs worldwide, caused by Ehrlichia canis and transmitted by the brown dog tick (Rhipicephalus sanguineus), ranges from mild illness to severe bleeding and organ failure. Historically highlighted during the Vietnam War when many military dogs died from a tropical pancytopenia. The disease has three phases: acute (2–4 weeks), subclinical (months–years with splenic persistence), and chronic. Chronic disease features thrombocytopenia with epistaxis, petechiae, ecchymoses, lameness from joint inflammation, and ocular involvement such as uveitis or retinal hemorrhages. Necropsy findings include splenomegaly and hepatomegaly; histology shows multisystem plasma cell infiltration, with bone marrow hypoplasia possible in chronic disease. Diagnosis combines clinical signs with hematology (thrombocytopenia, anemia, leukopenia) and serology (ELISA) and PCR; morulae in monocytes may be seen cytologically. Treatment is doxycycline for at least 28 days; severe cases need supportive therapy (transfusions, glucocorticoids). Prevention relies on vector control and regular ectoparasiticides; check dogs for ticks after outdoor exposure.

articleSummary: On 2026-03-19 at Hefei Xinqiao Airport, customs intercepted six dried yellow-breasted rats (total 0.205 kg) in a traveler’s checked baggage after green-channel screening; X-ray flagged the luggage and inspectors found sealed bags of six dried rats with an old, dry odor. Laboratory tests identified at least one dangerous pathogen in each rat: Leptospira, Ehrlichia, Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato, and Babesia. Yellow-breast rats commonly inhabit sewers and dark corners and can carry multiple bacteria and parasites. Leptospira can injure liver and kidney, potentially causing renal failure, meningitis, or hemorrhage; Ehrlichia damages the immune system; Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato (Lyme borreliosis) can cause chronic skin lesions and neurologic/joint pain; Babesia destroys red blood cells, leading to high fever and fatigue. This case highlights the import risk of wildlife products harboring multiple pathogens; no human cases are reported in the article.
notes: 本件は野生動物製品（乾燥ネズミ）の違法持ち込み事案で、動物由来の複合感染病原体が検出されたもの。現時点で人間感染者は報告されていないが、複数の危険病原体（特にレプトスピラとボレリアブルグドルフェリ）が確認されている点で、国境検疫と野生動物製品規制の面で監視価値あり。今後の人間感染例の報告があればPICKUPへ格上げ検討。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Man working in the fields sustains a hand puncture from bamboo splinters and develops tetanus; spring farming safety precautions deserve greater attention.
articleHeadline: 男子干农活被竹屑刺伤手感染破伤风 春耕防护需重视
articleSummary: In Heyuan, Guangdong, a man sustained a hand puncture from bamboo splinters while fieldwork, neglected wound; days later developed trismus and respiratory failure and was diagnosed with tetanus and admitted to ICU. His daughter notes such injuries from wood splinters and thorny debris are common during spring farming, but initial neglect can lead to rapid deterioration. Doctors at Meizhou People's Hospital infectious diseases department warn that Clostridium tetani is widespread in feces and soil, and deeper or contaminated wounds raise infection risk. The incubation period is typically 3–21 days; tetanospasmin and tetanolysin toxins cause symptoms such as lockjaw and 'risus sardonicus,' progressing to generalized muscle spasms and possible death. Recently, several severe cases have been admitted. Preventive measures include wearing gloves and rubber boots, thorough wound cleaning and disinfection, and timely tetanus vaccination or antitoxin. Adults should receive a booster every 10 years; high-risk workers require reinforced protection.
notes: 破傷風は散発的な個別症例。サマリーに「最近、複数の重症例が入院」との記述があるが、具体的な流行規模・パターンの情報がなく、季節的な農業関連損傷からの感染事例の医学的情報提供と位置づけられる。対象国にはマッチするが、シグナルの定義（異常性、国際的懸念、管理困難性）を満たさない。

articleSummary: Mass cobia mortality in Ly Son Special Zone, Quang Ngai Province, Vietnam, is linked to extremely high Vibrio spp. density in fish tissue (2.4×10^7 MPN/g) and hypoxic water (DO 4.49–4.9 mg/L). Lab tests found no Viral Nervous Necrosis or parasites in two sampled fish, but Vibrio levels were elevated. The outbreak began around 5 April; by 10 April, over 40 of 57 cages were damaged with >90 tons dead, exceeding 16 billion VND in losses. Contributing factors include crowded anchorages limiting water flow and southwest monsoon–driven disturbances causing stress. Authorities urge continued surveillance, moving cages to areas with better current, maintaining DO >5 mg/L (pH 7.5–8.3), reducing stocking density, placing lime around cages, strict biosecurity, daily health checks, probiotics, vitamins and minerals, beta-glucan, net sanitation, and antibiotic treatment per approved guidelines, with withdrawal times. Dead fish should be disinfected and buried; harvest market-size fish to minimize losses.

articleHeadline: Responsible antibiotic use and diagnostic challenges in infectious diseases : studies in a resource-limited setting and a high-income setting
articleSummary: India (resource-limited) and Sweden (high-income) reveal antibiotic overuse and diagnostic gaps. In two Indian hospitals, ICU antibiotic use reached 4,843 of 6,141 patients (70%), while infection-associated diagnoses were recorded in under 25%. Pediatric antibiotic use for gastroenteritis, respiratory infections, enteric fever, viral fever, or unspecified fever was 84% (2,088) at the non-teaching hospital vs 44% (224) at the teaching hospital. Broad-spectrum antibiotics were common; only 37% (TH) and 24% (NTH) prescriptions complied with the national essential medicines list. From 2008–2017, prescribing for severe infections and second-/third-line antibiotics and fixed-dose combinations rose at the non-teaching hospital; the teaching hospital showed increases in second-/third-line and FDCs but stable overall prescribing. In Sweden, infective endocarditis (IE) showed: aortic valve vegetation with Enterococcus faecalis; mitral vegetation with group B/viridans streptococci; tricuspid vegetation with Staphylococcus aureus in IV drug users; perivalvular abscesses/CIED-IE with coagulase-negative staphylococci. Conclusion: diagnostics are limited in resource-limited settings, risking underdiagnosis; echocardiography is effective for IE care in high-income settings and could guide management elsewhere.
notes: 本記事はスウェーデンの大学による学位論文（avhandlingar.se）の要旨。インドとスウェーデンでの過去の抗生物質使用パターンと診断法の比較研究であり、現在のアウトブレイク検知ではない。記事サマリーで言及されている感染症（感染性心内膜炎、腸チフス等）は歴史的なケーススタディまたは医学的背景知識であり、新規または拡大する感染症イベントの報告ではない。シグナルとしてのピックアップ対象ではない。

articleHeadline: Inhaled Therapy Aims to Cut Severe Lung Infection Damage
articleSummary: NTU Singapore, in collaboration with China’s Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech) and Lipigon Pharmaceuticals AB (Sweden), is developing an inhaled therapy to reduce lung damage from severe infections. The treatment targets ANGPTL4, which rises during inflammatory lung stress and drives vascular leakage and fibrosis; delivered by inhalation, it acts directly in the lungs to preserve tissue while preserving immune defense. In preclinical studies for bacterial pneumonia and viral influenza, the therapy reduced lung inflammation and fluid buildup and improved breathing; in a pulmonary fibrosis model it lowered scarring. The program is advancing to non-human primate evaluation and IND-enabling development, advancing RNA-based approaches for respiratory diseases. Global burden is high: seasonal influenza affects up to 1 billion people yearly, with 3–5 million serious cases and 290,000–650,000 deaths; pneumonia remains a leading death cause. Singapore reports >10,000 pneumonia admissions annually.

articleSummary: As of 13 April 2026, Bandar Lampung City Agriculture Department reports no Foot-and-Mouth Disease (PMK) cases among livestock. articleSummary: National influenza positivity rose for three consecutive weeks (Mar 30–Apr 5, 2026) in China’s sentinel acute respiratory infection surveillance. articleSummary: Indonesia has not detected the Cicada Covid-19 variant, a lineage of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.3.2 first identified in Africa South Africa in November 2024, which by February 2026 had spread to 23 countries. Vaccination and prior infection confer stronger immunity, though the emergence of a new variant may affect protection levels. Indonesian public should stay vigilant but calm while health protocols continue.

articleHeadline: Nodavirus de mortalidad encubierta: qué es, síntomas y cómo evitar el contagio
articleSummary: Hidden-mortality nodavirus (CMNV), a Nodaviridae member affecting aquatic organisms, causes "silent deaths" in shrimp and crustaceans and was first detected in 2009 in China, primarily impacting Litopenaeus vannamei. It has since been documented across freshwater, brackish, and marine ecosystems in farmed and wild species, heightening aquaculture risk. A Nature Communications study led by University College London finds indications of a possible interspecies jump toward humans, potentially linked to anterior viral hypertensive uveitis. About 71.4% of patients reported direct contact with aquatic animals, suggesting exposure via handling or consuming undercooked seafood. In humans, ocular symptoms include persistent blurred vision, redness, pain, and light sensitivity; severe cases may cause inflammation and elevated intraocular pressure with risk of irreversible vision loss if untreated. CMNV is not yet formally classified by OIE; no curative treatment exists, so prevention—water disinfection, surveillance, and strict aquaculture sanitation—is essential.
notes: 記事は水生生物由来のノダウイルスのヒトへの種間越境を示唆するが、確認患者数、臨床的な証拠の強度、OIE/WHOの公式認識がいずれも記載されていない。University College London による研究への言及があるが、査読状況や発表時期が不明。水産物を通じた露出リスク（71.4%が水生動物との直接接触）は継続的な曝露リスクを示す。中国での初期検出（2009年）と現在の国際的分布が記載されているが、ヒト症例が実際に複数国で確認されたかは不明確。引き続き公式な感染症情報源（WHO、CDC、中国CDC）からの確認を待つべき。

articleSummary: Takeda Vietnam intensifies dengue prevention in Vietnam with DeRIGHT-V, a platform campaign to demystify dengue. articleHeadline: Impact of intensive control on malaria population genomics under elimination settings in Southeast Asia - Nature Microbiology
articleSummary: Plasmodium falciparum in Kayin State, eastern Myanmar, under the SMRU-led METF malaria elimination program, shows extreme clonal expansion under drug pressure. From 2015–2020, 5,014 dried blood spots were collected; genome-wide sequencing of 2,270 samples yielded 1,927 P. falciparum genomes with 25,461 high-quality SNPs, and 92.4% were single-genotype infections. 93 IBD clusters (2–229 samples) plus 73 singletons formed 166 unique genomes; genetic richness R ranged 0.10–0.30, indicating very low diversity. The ten largest IBD clusters accounted for 51.6% of infections; 91.0% of genomes were related (r≥0.25) to others, reflecting high inbreeding and limited outbreeding (mean cluster duration ~13.8 months; family duration ~48.7 months). Spatial structure shows localized transmission, with clusters centered around Hpapun Township and relatedness strongest within ≤20 km; negative correlations appear between 27.5–90 km, delineating cluster boundaries. kelch13 mutations R561H, F446I, P441L observed, indicating ongoing drug selection pressure.
notes: 記事はNature Microbiology掲載の査読済み学術論文。2015-2020年のカイン州での根絶プログラム下での遺伝学的解析結果。kelch13突然変異による薬剤耐性選択圧が検出されているが、これは既知のプログラム内での継続的な遺伝的監視の一部。新規感染症危機ではなく、ゲノム監視の重要性を示す研究報告。

The Ministério Público do Amapá (MP-AP) is guiding and monitoring responses without direct action, with Promoters Wueber Penafort and Fábia Nilci coordinating health-defense efforts and convening state and municipal representatives to align strategies and demand effective measures. Cases are concentrated in the southern districts of Zerão, Universidade, Congós, and Buritizal. The MP recommends intensified sanitary oversight, especially of the acai production chain, worker training, and public education campaigns. Pará state experiences, including an interinstitutional plan and acai-beater training, are being leveraged. Actions underway include trainings for health professionals and community agents from April 14, seminars for acai beaters, and expanded inspections. A technical note on clinical management is being drafted to speed diagnosis and treatment.

articleHeadline: Salmonella na suinocultura: "não é uma doença, é um ecossistema dentro da granja", alerta especialista
articleSummary: As of 2026, Salmonella in swine farming is a structural problem in modern pig production. Surveys show high prevalence across production systems, with monophasic Salmonella Typhimurium accounting for about 42.5% of isolates and Salmonella Choleraesuis about 33%. Multidrug resistance is widespread, with MDR strains exceeding 90% and up to 94.7% in some profiles. Salmonella operates as an on-farm ecosystem—present in the environment, animals, feed and water, with many asymptomatic carriers—requiring integrated, data-driven control. In challenged herds, nursery mortality can exceed 10–14%; vaccination reduces excretion, infection pressure and clinical/subclinical impacts. Vaccines targeting the intestinal tract that stimulate cellular immunity are emphasized. Gel-based administration improves dose distribution and operational efficiency for large-scale programs, especially in suckling piglets. Slaughter findings show reductions of over 80% in positive lymph nodes, enhancing food safety.
notes: 記事はブラジルの養豚業におけるサルモネラ菌の農場レベルでの構造的問題と制御戦略について述べているもので、ヒトの疾病発生事例ではない。影響カテゴリが「environment」と「animals」に限定され、ヒト感染症の爆発的流行や公衆衛生上の緊急事態を示唆する内容ではない。したがって感染症危機管理の対象外と判定。

articleSummary: Measles cases in Indonesia are rising as of 2026-04-13, with thousands of confirmed infections and dozens of fatalities in early 2026. articleSummary: As of 13 April 2026, China’s national influenza sentinel surveillance shows the influenza-positive rate rising for three consecutive weeks, higher in northern provinces than the south, with influenza B now the dominant circulating strain. The upsurge follows a peak of influenza B in Dec 2023–Jan 2024; waning population immunity and spring temperature fluctuations likely contribute, alongside increased outdoor activity and crowding. Influenza B tends to cause more gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea) than influenza A, with children and adolescents disproportionately affected. Early antiviral treatment (within 48 hours) with oseltamivir or baloxavir marboxil reduces severe outcomes and shortening of illness; high-risk groups (elderly, pregnant women, those with chronic diseases) benefit even after 48 hours. Vaccination remains the main preventive measure; current trivalent and quadrivalent vaccines cover A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B strains, though immunity wanes since winter, suggesting spring booster if feasible. Preventive tips include masking, hand hygiene, avoiding crowded places, and prompt testing for timely antiviral use.

articleHeadline: Siapa yang Rentan Terinfeksi Campak Berulang? Ini Penjelasan Dokter
articleSummary: Measles remains a concern in Indonesia, affecting both children and adults, with possible reinfection when immunity wanes or when the initial diagnosis was incorrect. Immunity can arise naturally after infection or via vaccination, but protection is not absolute; vaccination reduces the risk of severe disease or death but does not guarantee full protection against infection. Recurrent measles is theoretically possible but rare. Pediatric specialist Aisya Fikritama notes that a true long-term antibody response usually follows infection, potentially preventing future disease; however, if the initial diagnosis was wrong, people may have had rubella, roseola, or another rash-causing virus, leading to viral exanthem and no real measles immunity. Statements from Indonesian health officials in early April 2026 underscore the need for accurate diagnosis and continued vaccination to mitigate outbreaks.

articleSummary: WHO is monitoring a new Covid-19 variant named Cicada, identified as BA.3.2. The WHO classifies BA.3.2 as 'under surveillance' pending further study of its potential public-health impact. articleSummary: Da Nang, a city in central Vietnam, faces a rising hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) outbreak. articleHeadlineTranslated: Signs of meningococcal disease that are easy to miss.

articleSummary: Vietnam reports 24 meningococcal disease cases this year, including 4 deaths, up 14 cases from the same period in 2025. Neisseria meningitidis spreads rapidly by respiratory droplets or nasal/oropharyngeal secretions; humans are the only reservoir. Close contacts have markedly higher risk—up to 500–800 times. About 10–20% of people carry the bacteria in the throat, rising to 25–32% among teens and up to 50% during outbreaks. Fulminant disease classically presents as meningitis or septicemia with sudden high fever, neck stiffness, vomiting, severe pain, and rash, potentially fatal within 24 hours if untreated. Atypical forms include pneumonia, arthritis, pericarditis, conjunctivitis, otitis, sinusitis, urethritis, and proctitis; bacteremia can occur without meningitis signs and may persist for at least a week. Vaccines cover serogroups A, B, C, W, Y. In Vietnam, MenQuadfi, Nimenrix, Menactra (ACYW); Bexsero; combined B and C vaccines are licensed; boosters advised for BC or AC groups.
notes: 脳膜炎菌疾患は24時間以内に致命的となる可能性がある。ベトナムでの2026年の症例増加と死亡が報告されており、重症度が高い。呼吸器飛沫による人人感染が主な伝播経路で、ハイリスク接触者は500～800倍のリスクを有する。IHR基準3項目以上該当およびWPRO基準4項目該当でPICKUP判定。

Vo Hai Son, deputy director of the Vietnam Administration of Disease Prevention, warned that dengue infections could continue to rise if prevention and control measures are not implemented strictly and consistently. The health sector is working with local authorities to monitor and contain outbreaks and is stepping up public communication on disease prevention. No lab-confirmed details, infection source beyond mosquito breeding, or mention of imported/exported cases are provided. articleSummary: As of 2026-04-14, Vietnam faces concurrent outbreaks of hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) and dengue fever. About 26,000 HFMD cases have caused 8 pediatric deaths, and nearly 32,000 dengue cases have led to 4 deaths nationwide. Laboratory surveillance detects circulation of the enterovirus 71 (EV71) strain, increasing risk of severe complications in children. The southern region is hardest hit, with Ho Chi Minh City reporting 1,347 new HFMD cases last week—64% above the four-week average—lifting the year-to-date total above 10,000 and prompting hospitals to activate high-level outbreak responses and add hundreds of beds. Dengue is appearing earlier than expected due to climate variability and urban density, with Aedes breeding in home water containers. Public health urges weekly removal of standing water, covering and cleaning containers, and personal protection. For HFMD, emphasize early detection, isolation, and school exclusions to curb spread.
notes: 手足口病26,000人（小児死亡8人）、デング熱32,000人（死亡4人）の同時流行。EV71株の検出により重症化リスクが高い。ホーチミン市で4週間平均比64%増の急増を記録。両疾病ともに環境要因（気候変動、水容器でのシマカ繁殖）と人口密集が悪化要因として指摘されている。
